result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give the same core advice: no loader on the fast path, one skeleton only after a ~200 ms delay, a minimum display time, keeping previous results visible, and never stacking two loaders. B edges ahead on what matters beyond the loader: a manual-entry fallback so checkout is never blocked, specific screen-reader announcements, aria-hidden skeleton rows, debouncing and reduced motion. A is a bit tighter and easier to act on, and neither answer covers keyboard use of the list. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): The two answers are nearly equivalent: each says to show neither loader by default, delay a single skeleton until the lookup has run for a short while, set a minimum display time, keep stale results visible, and use aria-live. A wins narrowly because it covers the failure case better for checkout: on error it offers manual address entry, never blocks checkout, and respects reduced motion. B's suggestion of an inline spinner as a compromise slightly blurs its recommendation, and neither answer covers keyboard use of the list.
